evidence.claim: Exact tool pins, compatibility results, trust-boundary audit draft and a provisional ISA/toolchain pin (sections 1-9, Wave A); section 10 records the Wave B proofs below and what they trust; section 11 records the Wave C decode coverage, bridge, EL0 attempt and coqchk. Exact 152-byte tarm64le code object from plain Chez 10.3.0 for Shen-Scheme v0.52's generated form of (define buri-arm-add X Y -> (+ X Y)); one relocated instance; executed under qemu-aarch64 only.
Exact 680-byte code component produced inside Shen-CL 4844072d on aarch64 SBCL 2.6.8; executed under qemu-aarch64 only.
x86_64 only: in-process Shen-Scheme v0.52 code equals plain Chez 10.3.0 code modulo three relocated addresses, for one function.
isla e9b5d945 symbolic execution of the Sail Armv9.4-A IR on the exact opcode bytes; trusts isla, z3 and the Sail-to-IR translation; not checked by Rocq.

Checked by opt-in scripts/check-arm.sh (Coq 8.18.0, stdpp 1.10.0, coq-sail 0.19, sail-arm 7d058164 Armv9.4 Coq model; not in scripts/prove). Universal over pc: the model's __DecodeA64 on the captured Chez word 0xab010017 (+0x14) equals read SEE; if SEE < 15 then write SEE 15 and execute ADDS X23,X0,X1 else throw Error_Undefined; that execute equals an explicit register-transfer program; under SEE < 15 the decoder admits the sequential trace writing PSTATE.NZCV and X23 := (X0+X1) mod 2^64. Decoder statements inherit the model's three Coq-stdlib Reals axioms; execute and sum lemmas are closed. One data-processing word only.

Separate Coq 8.19.0 environment with stdpp a1a12e00, Iris 6f24ed4b, Lithium 7945a29d, record-update 0.3.3, isla-lang bda86c9f and Islaris c978e10f, fetched by exact git commit from GitHub mirrors; built here, and Islaris's own examples/example.v checks in it. Deviations: dune 3.23.1, ott 0.34.

Checked by ports/arm/islaris/check-islaris.sh in the Coq 8.19.0 environment; closed under the global context. For all fixnum-tagged a, b without signed overflow, with X23 = 2 and an aligned frame slot holding ra, the Chez fast path +0x00..+0x23 (captured bytes) reaches ra with X23 = a+b, X30 = a|b, X10 = ra; slow paths proved infeasible. Relative to Islaris's semantics of isla b8e614bd (and e9b5d945) traces of the Armv8.5 IR under Islaris's EL2/MMU-off constraints, not the Armv9.4 Coq model and not EL0 Linux; trace = architecture is trusted to isla and z3.

Checked by opt-in scripts/check-arm.sh Part B (Coq 8.19.0 Islaris env, coq-sail 0.19, sail-arm 7d058164 Armv9.4 Coq model rebuilt in 8.19.0; not in scripts/prove). Universal over pc: exact iMon equations for __DecodeA64 on twelve captured words, each bound to the stored bytes: Chez +0x00 cmp, +0x04/+0x10 b.ne, +0x08 orr, +0x0c tst, +0x18 b.vs, +0x1c ldur (load), +0x20 br, +0x2c str (store); SBCL +0x210 ret (return), +0x2a0 blr x10 (call to ALLOC-TRAMP), +0x264 brk #15 (trap). Each fixes encoding, SEE guard, decoder register reads and exact execute arguments; execute-side behaviour (memory, BranchTo, exception entry) is NOT covered. Decoder statements inherit the model's three Coq-stdlib Reals axioms; three auxiliary equations are closed. A modified word (b.eq) is rejected.

Checked by opt-in scripts/check-arm.sh Part B in one Coq 8.19.0 with both Islaris opsem and the Armv9.4 model. chez_0014_bridge (universal over pc, SEE<15, X0, X1, PSTATE, prior PC/R23): the model's decoder on 0xab010017 admits its unique register trace AND the Islaris trace a14.v used by buri_chez_add_fast_path (isla b8e614bd, Armv8.5 IR) runs to completion under Islaris's seq_step, never blocking, to the map with R23 = the model's AddWithCarry result, PSTATE.NZCV = the model's flags and _PC += 4 (a14_run and the bit lemmas closed under the global context). Covers one word only; the trace's PC step versus the model's __InstructionExecute PC advance, the converse direction, and the other eight fast-path words are not bridged. A trace with bvadd replaced by bvxor is rejected.

EL0/stage-1-MMU-on (Linux non-VHE) isla b8e614bd footprints of the Chez fast path: 8 of 9 words traced (data-processing identical to EL2; branches add a TBI0 top-byte split), ldur resource-exhausted (killed twice, 7 GiB cap on the second run; no trace). No EL0 Islaris proof exists. Unchecked isla output, not a theorem.

Section 11.5: coqchk -o of SailArm.armv9 (Coq 8.19.0 build, all dependencies) passes in 3 min 18 s at 1.0 GB; context axioms are the model's six external memory/sleep primitives and five Coq-stdlib axioms, none from Buri. check-arm.sh Part B re-runs coqchk over BuriArmDecode and BuriArmBridge.
